MFA.No.22286/2011 and MFA.No.22287/2011 are filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 04.01.2011 in MVC.Nos.286/2009 and 322/2009 passed by the District Judge (Fast Track) & MACT, Haveri, questioning the liability fastened on the owner of the TATA Sumo to pay compensation and also for enhancement of compensation.
2. The factum of accident is not in dispute.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.

Learned counsel for the claimants submitted that the Tribunal has committed error that the TATA Sumo vehicle is not involved in the accident, but falsely implicated into the case and the owner of the TATA Sumo has admitted that his vehicle was involved in the accident and fastening liability on the owner is not correct.
P.W.3 is the eye witness and he has deposed that the TATA Sumo has caused the accident resulting into death of two NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 persons.
Further submitted that the Insurance Company has not challenged the charge sheet.
Further submitted that the result in criminal case does not have any impact on the claim proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act.
5. Further submitted that in the written statement the Insurance Company has admitted the accident and also the involvement of TATA Sumo vehicle.
Further submitted that the Insurance Company has not examined the Investigating Officer or any other witnesses to disprove that the TATA Sumo vehicle is not involved in the accident.

Further the evidence in the claim proceedings are to be appreciated on the theory of preponderance of probabilities, but not beyond reasonable doubt, but the Tribunal has adopted the recourse of principle of beyond reasonable doubt in coming to the conclusion that the TATA Sumo is not involved in the accident and that is permissible.
Therefore, submitted that the Tribunal has erroneously fastened liability on the owner of the TATA Sumo and also prays for enhancement of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 compensation.

Therefore,
submitted that when the claimants have proved from the charge sheet materials and from the evidence of P.W.3 who is the eye witness, it is proved that the TATA Sumo vehicle was involved in the accident.
Therefore, prays for modification of the liability and also for enhancement of compensation.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company submitted that on 17.03.2007 the accident was caused, but the vehicle was alleged to have seized on 13.06.2007 after three months from the date of accident and for which, there is no cogent material as to how the Investigating Officer came to know that the TATA Sumo vehicle was involved in the accident.
In the complaint, the nature / type or number of offending vehicle is not stated.

Further submitted that P.W.3, even though, is stated to be eye witness, but his evidence is not found to be believable and Neelawwa W/O. Hanumantappa ... vs Nagaraj F Gawali on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109576587/

his evidence is not trust worthy.

Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly rejected the evidence of P.W.3.
7.

Further submitted that the claimants and P.W.3 have turned hostile in the criminal case and therefore, since the real vehicle which has caused the accident was not traced out, hence TATA Sumo vehicle was falsely implicated into the case only for the purpose of making claim against the Insurance Company upon finding the TATA Sumo vehicle was having insurance policy and the driver was holding driving licence.

Therefore, submitted that upon considering all the eventualities,
it is proved that the TATA Sumo has not caused the accident and hence, justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

8. The Tribunal has observed and concluded that the TATA Sumo vehicle is not involved in the accident and was falsely implicated into the case, but the owner has admitted that his TATA Sumo vehicle was involved in the NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 accident.
Therefore, fastened liability on the owner of the TATA Sumo vehicle.
The accident was caused in the midnight at 1:15 a.m., on 17.03.2007.
In the said accident two persons died.
P.W.3 is stated to be eye witness, but he has not lodged the complaint before the police, but another person has lodged the complaint before the police.

It is the evidence of P.W.3 that he was knocking his door at 1:15 a.m., and at that time, TATA Sumo vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-25/M-3016 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motor cycle on which the deceased were traveling as rider and pillion rider on the motorcycle.
Further it is the evidence of P.W.3 that within 15 to 20 minutes police and other persons arrived to the spot of accident.
When this being the evidence of P.W.3 that he has witnessed the accident, but he has not lodged the complaint before the police
. This conduct of P.W.3 is found to be suspicious.

From the charge sheet materials, it is borne out that P.W.3 has given statement before the Investigating Officer that he has witnessed the accident by NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 mentioning the nature of vehicle as TATA Sumo.
Whether P.W.3 went himself voluntarily to give statement before the police or the police had come to P.W.3 for taking statement is not forthcoming.
This observation is very important to see the conduct of PW.3.
PW.3 has also given evidence before the Criminal Court, but he turned hostile.

From turning hostile in criminal case resulting acquittal of accused even though, does not have any impact on the claim proceedings, but this aspect is to be considered in the background of the contention raised by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that TATA Sumo vehicle is falsely implicated into the case.
The evidence in the claim proceedings are to be considered on the theory of preponderance of probabilities, but not by adopting the theory of beyond reasonable doubt.
What would be the probability value by considering the evidence on record and getting impression as to what would have been probabilized in proving the facts in issue is to be considered.
The claimants have also turned hostile.
PW.3 is stated to be eye-witness has also turned hostile in the criminal case before the Court of J.M.F.C.

Therefore, preponderance of probability involved in Neelawwa W/O. Hanumantappa ... vs Nagaraj F Gawali on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109576587/

sentences.text: the case is considered the conduct of PW.3 is also to be appreciated in the background for the contents raised by the Insurance Company of involving the Tata Sumo vehicle otherwise the conduct of eye-witness in claim proceedings cannot be significant.

Section 8 of the Indian Evidence Act,
1872, reads regarding motive, preparation and conduct etc., of the witness whether, the said witness is found to be relevant or not.
Relevancy is a relative turn used in the Evidence Act.
One fact is relevant to another fact and therefore, if fact is relevant to another fact, then the question of admissibility is to be considered.
Here the relevancy means the conduct of PW.3 that is witness to the accident.
Therefore, the relevancy in the present case is proving of factum of accident and involvement of vehicles and seeing the said accident by PW.3.

But upon considering the conduct of PW.3, in the background of the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 defence raised by the Insurance Company that Tata Sumo vehicle is falsely implicated, the evidence of PW.3 is not found to be relevant that he has witnessed the accident.
PW.3 has not lodged complaint before the police and has not given statement before the police soon after the accident.
If PW.3 voluntarily went to the investigating officer and stated that he has witnessed the accident within reasonable period from the date of accident that would have been relevant.
But the records revealed that the statement of PW.3 was recorded by the investigating officer after 15 days from the date of the accident.
Therefore, the relevancy regarding chain of all events is to be considered.
But the fact remains proved that PW.3 has turned hostile in the criminal case but supported in the claim proceedings before the Tribunal.

This observation assumes importance that why there might not have been chances that owner of Tata Sumo vehicle might have colluded with claimants for claiming compensation against the Insurance Company.
Therefore, all these aspects are to be considered.

The Tata Sumo vehicle was seized on 13.06.2007 after three months from the date of the accident and on the very same day, every formality in the course of investigation is completed and filed charge sheet.
This fact and circumstance is to be seen while considering evidence on all its preponderance of probability.
11. The driver and owner of the Tata Sumo have stated that the Tata Sumo vehicle was involved in the accident.

Just because the owner and driver have stated that the Tata Sumo vehicle has caused accident, it can be viewed in the context of possibility of colluding the owner with claimants for the purpose of making claim against the Insurance Company.

Therefore, after considering the entire evidence on record on all its preponderance of probability as above discussed, the Tribunal is correct in holding that the Tata Sumo vehicle is falsely implicated in the case.

But the Tribunal had held that the owner of the Tata Sumo vehicle liable to pay compensation for the - 13 - Neelawwa W/O. Hanumantappa ... vs Nagaraj F Gawali on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109576587/
6 NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 reason that the owner had admitted that his Tata Sumo vehicle was involved in the accident.

sentences.text: Therefore, on all these admissions of the owner, the Tribunal has directed the owner to pay compensation and is found to be justified that the owner stated voluntarily his vehicle was involved in the accident.
12. The another contention raised by the learned counsel for the claimants that the Insurance Company has not challenged charge sheet.
For the Insurance Company there is no occasion to challenge the charge sheet.
It is not the duty cast on the Insurance Company to challenge the charge sheet.
The charge sheet is filed for the purpose of foisting charge sheet of offence against the accused alleging that the accused has committed offence punishable under statutes.
Many at times, the insurance company does not have locus-standi to challenge the charge sheet.
Also it cannot be expected the insurance company to challenge charge sheet in each and every cases as it is not domain of the charge sheet.

Therefore,
- 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 the submission canvassed that the insurance company has not challenged charge sheet is absurd and ridicule.
Just because the Insurance Company has not challenged the charge sheet, does not mean that the Insurance Company has admitted regarding involvement of vehicle.
The case is considered on preponderance of probabilities.

Just because in the charge sheet,
the offending vehicle is mentioned that always is not gospel truth regarding involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
The evidence produced before the Tribunal is to be considered independently without being influenced by the findings of the criminal Court.

In the present case,
the accident is occurred on 17.03.2007 and the Tata Sumo vehicle was seized on 13.06.2007 after three months.
It is the defence of the Insurance Company that Tata Sumo vehicle is not involved in the accident.

Though, the Insurance Company has taken pleadings in the written statement that Tata Sumo vehicle has caused accident but in the claim proceedings strict rules of evidence and pleadings are not applicable.
The aspects of involvement of vehicle is to be - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 considered on all its preponderance of probabilities without being influenced by findings in Criminal Court.

Pleadings in the claim proceedings are only for giving necessary information to the tribunal for coming to just conclusion regarding factum of accident,
involvement of vehicle and rash and negligent aspect, injury sustained/death occurred and entitlement of compensation by the parties and nothing more than that.
Therefore, in the back ground of the defence raised by insurer of the Tata Sumo vehicle is falsely implicated into the case.

PW.3 has not lodged complaint before the police and even though he was eye witness in the charge sheet but in the criminal proceedings he has turned hostile but has given evidence before the Tribunal in this claim proceeding that he has witnessed the accident, by stating that Tata Sumo vehicle has caused accident.
This conduct of PW.3 probablise the fact that creating doubtfulness regarding involvement of Tata Sumo vehicle in the accident.

Therefore, the Tribunal is justified in observing that the Tata Sumo vehicle was falsely implicated, but because of the fact that the owner Neelawwa W/O. Hanumantappa ... vs Nagaraj F Gawali on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109576587/
7 - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 admitted the accident, fastened liability on the owner of the Tata Sumo vehicle.
Therefore, this finding of fact made by the Tribunal need not to interfered with.

Therefore,
on all these aspects, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is liable to be confirmed, so far as liability.

dead body 3. Towards funeral charges Rs.10,000/-

14. In the present case, the deceased was aged 40 years and was a mechanic, died in the accident caused on 17.03.2007.

The Tribunal has taken the income as Rs.3,000/-
which is on lower side.

Therefore, as per the chart of notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, a sum of Rs.4,000/- per month to be taken as notional monthly income of the - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 deceased.
The Tribunal has not added income towards loss of future prospects in life.

According to the age of the deceased, 25% of the income is to be added towards 'Loss of Future Prospects' as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1, i.e., Rs.1,000/- (Rs.4,000 x 25%).

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Relevancy is a relative turn used in the Evidence Act.
One fact is relevant to another fact and therefore, if fact is relevant to another fact, then the question of admissibility is to be considered.
Here the relevancy means the conduct of PW.3 that is witness to the accident.
Therefore, the relevancy in the present case is proving of factum of accident and involvement of vehicles and seeing the said accident by PW.3.
But upon considering the conduct of PW.3, in the background of the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8839 defence raised by the Insurance Company that Tata Sumo vehicle is falsely implicated, the evidence of PW.3 is not found to be relevant that he has witnessed the accident.
Just because the owner and driver have stated that the Tata Sumo vehicle has caused accident, it can be viewed in the context of possibility of colluding the owner with claimants for the purpose of making claim against the Insurance Company.
Therefore, after considering the entire evidence on record on all its preponderance of probability as above discussed, the Tribunal is correct in holding that the Tata Sumo vehicle is falsely implicated in the case.
It is not the duty cast on the Insurance Company to challenge the charge sheet.
The charge sheet is filed for the purpose of foisting charge sheet of offence against the accused alleging that the accused has committed offence punishable under statutes.
Many at times, the insurance company does not have locus-standi to challenge the charge sheet.
Also it cannot be expected the insurance company to challenge charge sheet in each and every cases as it is not domain of the charge sheet.
Just because the Insurance Company has not challenged the charge sheet, does not mean that the Insurance Company has admitted regarding involvement of vehicle.
The case is considered on preponderance of probabilities.
Just because in the charge sheet,
the offending vehicle is mentioned that always is not gospel truth regarding involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
The evidence produced before the Tribunal is to be considered independently without being influenced by the findings of the criminal Court.
In the present case,
the accident is occurred on 17.03.2007 and the Tata Sumo vehicle was seized on 13.06.2007 after three months.
It is the defence of the Insurance Company that Tata Sumo vehicle is not involved in the accident.
Though, the Insurance Company has taken pleadings in the written statement that Tata Sumo vehicle has caused accident but in the claim proceedings strict rules of evidence and pleadings are not applicable.
Pleadings in the claim proceedings are only for giving necessary information to the tribunal for coming to just conclusion regarding factum of accident,
involvement of vehicle and rash and negligent aspect, injury sustained/death occurred and entitlement of compensation by the parties and nothing more than that.
PW.3 has not lodged complaint before the police and even though he was eye witness in the charge sheet but in the criminal proceedings he has turned hostile but has given evidence before the Tribunal in this claim proceeding that he has witnessed the accident, by stating that Tata Sumo vehicle has caused accident.
This conduct of PW.3 probablise the fact that creating doubtfulness regarding involvement of Tata Sumo vehicle in the accident.
The Tribunal has not added income towards loss of future prospects in life.
